## Outcome and evidence

Does the fully dissociated model reproduce the paper's calculated curves and how does it compare with measured symbols?
[Held, Cameretti and Sadowski (2008)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fluid.2008.06.010), Figures 1–8, supplies the model lines and measured symbols separately.
Agreement is partial. Density differences and vapor pressures are generally closer to the printed curves than several mean ionic activity curves.
Admitted disjoint source rectangles remain failed reproductions; their thermodynamic cause is undetermined where the convention probes do not isolate it.
Model-line comparisons are numerical verification. Measured-symbol comparisons are physical comparison within figure reading precision, with no claim of physical validation or experimental uncertainty.

## Source ownership correction and scope

The final source selection corrects the guide errors identified in delivered r2:
CsBr density in Figure 2, lower LiI water-coefficient ink in Figure 4a,
and upper CsOH ionic-coefficient ink in Figure 7. The original crops and
every prior guide rejection were inspected without consulting Engine
residuals. [guide-corrections.csv](inputs/source/guide-corrections.csv) records
the local guide ordinates and the explicit reasons for remaining exclusions.
Original pixel coordinates, source ordinates, abscissa intervals and reading
allowances are unchanged. The same competing-guide check still applies.

Figure 4a assigns its lower, middle and upper dotted curves to LiI, NaI and
KI; Figure 4b assigns them to NaI, NaBr and NaCl. These assignments follow
the visible ion labels and marker shapes, correcting the interchanged verbal
caption. Figure 6 runs LiBr, NaBr, KBr, RbBr and CsBr from upper to lower
separated activity curves; Figure 7 runs CsOH, KOH, NaOH and LiOH. Low-molality
coincidences do not yield independently owned curves. Previously rejected
KI and RbBr neighbouring-ink witnesses remain excluded. Two additional
RbBr edge selections could not be separated from the nearby CsBr stroke
and are now excluded explicitly, preserving their native values.

The revised source selection was frozen before reclassification. The
comparison-only command reads the original native interval samples and
uses the existing overlap rule; a missing retained sample stops the command.
It performs no model evaluation. Tables 3–5 and the complete native results
remain unchanged. The [curation record](results/source-curation.json) links
both source hashes to the original execution; [every changed disposition](results/source-curation-changes.csv)
preserves its earlier result. The earlier disclosed delivery under #733 is
historical. This corrected selection awaits independent delivered review
and investigator promotion; sparse correlated pixels and remaining source
exclusions still prevent a complete source-coverage or aggregate-accuracy claim.

## Physical basis, conditions and source limits

The declared packet is `held-cameretti-sadowski-2008/4`: complete dissociation, water-only vapor, hard chain, dispersion, water association and Debye–Hückel; no Born term.
Held's printed screening diameter is sigma; the separately sourced packing diameter is reduced as stated in Held et al. (2014), Eq. (21).
Ion–ion dispersion exclusions, water parameters and its temperature-dependent diameter remain those of the packet.
The packet's primary activity temperature and permittivity remain unchanged.
Off-temperature results are conditional on [Ascani and Held (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1002/zaac.202100032), Table 5, water row, p.1309. This is not an exact replay of the authors' unstated dielectric law.

Off-temperature dielectric supplements

## Digitization and numerical criteria

Every legible centre is separate from model ink. Manual guides and a second source-ink lane use the original crop coordinates, calibrated axis endpoints and checked midpoint ticks.
Marker masks, annotations, touching axes and coincident low-concentration strokes have named causes in `figure-extraction.csv`; hidden coordinates are not inferred.
Candidates must lie within three vertical source pixels of their locally corrected guide and be more than two pixels closer to it than any competing guide at the same column. Source-inspected marker, axis and coincident-stroke exclusions remain review cases; no-ink columns remain gaps. The original guide is retained alongside each correction. Source-only checks for every series are in [the ownership recheck](inputs/source/figure-ownership-recheck.csv), with [gap locations](inputs/source/figure-gaps.csv). Shared ink remains excluded from agreement. The provisional Figure 4b anchors are retained only as historical anchors.
Printed decimals use half the last printed unit; counts require exact equality. Figure rectangles have three original-source pixels of half-width per axis; these are reading criteria.
Native predictions use the central abscissa, interval endpoints and fixed quarter-interval interior samples. Agreement requires ordinate-interval overlap with a continuous native range, preserving direction.
Disjoint sampled ranges on locally monotone branches fail; intervals with unresolved turning extrema remain undetermined. Five samples do not provide a global extremum certificate.
The water coefficient is only the permitted reporting normalization $\gamma_w=a_w/x_w$; its arithmetic identity supplies no independent thermodynamic test.

## Bounded convention diagnosis and execution

Shortening the Debye–Hückel screening diameter while retaining the packing diameter lowers the ionic coefficient and raises the water coefficient in the evaluated cases. This reduces the source-curve differences for the hydroxides and several cesium salts, and worsens the LiBr, NaBr and KBr differences. The corrected-source comparisons also worsen CsNO3 and RbCl overall. The printed screening convention remains the primary declaration. The remaining disagreement with the paper's own curves is unresolved after the stated basis, reference, term and temperature checks; it is not attributed to omitted ion pairing or physical-model inaccuracy.

The labelled shorter-screening probe uses the same source-selected abscissae, reading intervals and exclusions as the primary declaration for every activity model line, including the failing series. It is a departure from the printed screening statement, not evidence of Held's historical executable convention. The earlier fixed probes, including fixed off-temperature dielectric checks, remain in `results/diagnostics.json`.

Held 2008 Eqs. (8)–(10) use formula-unit molality with total ion stoichiometry. The native molal coefficient conversion, infinite-dilution references at the same temperature and pressure, and terminal reference changes were checked in the delivered review and are retained with the native records. The screening and packing lengths are separate. Room-temperature activity runs keep the packet dielectric; only off-temperature runs use the conditional supplement. Equation (1) contains no Born term. Native same-sign exclusions and packet unlike-ion dispersion suppression remain applied, with water–ion binary coefficients unchanged. Water coefficients retain the native composition and the accepted reporting division. These checks establish no declaration defect; they do not identify the remaining cause of disagreement.

The source-confirmed high-molality CsCl case below still misses with either screening declaration. An Engine defect would require disagreement with the governing equations or an independent implementation under identical declarations; the paper-curve discrepancy alone does not establish one.

```{python}
probes = pd.read_csv(root/'results/convention-probes.csv')

errors = probes[probes.qa.eq('pass') & probes.molality.ge(1)].groupby(['figure','panel','salt','mode']).signed_error.agg(mean_signed_error='mean', mean_absolute_error=lambda x: x.abs().mean())
table(counts.join(errors).reset_index())
table(probes[probes.figure.eq(5) & probes.salt.eq('CsCl') & probes.molality.eq(4.875)][['salt','temperature_K','molality','molality_half_width','value','value_half_width','mode','native_value','signed_error','outcome']])
```
